name: Dropzone

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code:
<Dropzone
  label="Attachments"
  name="attachments"
  multiple
  icon={<Icon name="upload" />}
  hint="Any files, as many as you like"
/>

examples.title: One File of One Type
examples.code:
<Dropzone
  label="CV"
  name="cv"
  accept=".pdf,application/pdf"
  maxSize={5_000_000}
  hint="PDF up to 5 MB"
  required
/>

examples.title: Several Files, Up to a Limit
examples.code:
<Dropzone
  label="Photos"
  name="photos"
  multiple
  maxFiles={5}
  accept="image/*"
  icon={<Icon name="images" />}
  buttonLabel="Choose or drop photos"
  hint="Up to 5 images"
/>

examples.title: In a Form
Controlled
Refusals
examples.code:
<Dropzone
  label="Spreadsheet"
  accept=".csv,text/csv"
  maxSize={1_000_000}
  hint="One CSV up to 1 MB"
  rejectionMessage={({ file, code }) =>
    code === 'file-too-large'
      ? `${file.name} is over 1 MB. Try splitting it.`
      : code === 'file-invalid-type'
        ? `${file.name} isn't a CSV.`
        : `${file.name}: one file at a time.`
  }
  onReject={rejections => console.log(rejections)}
/>

examples.title: In Another Language
examples.code:
<LocaleProvider locale="de">
  <Dropzone
    label="Anhänge"
    multiple
    buttonLabel="Dateien wählen oder ablegen"
    hint="Beliebige Dateien"
    removeLabel={file => `${file.name} entfernen`}
    addedMessage={files =>
      files.length === 1
        ? `${files[0].name} hinzugefügt`
        : `${files.length} Dateien hinzugefügt`
    }
    removedMessage={file => `${file.name} entfernt`}
    rejectionMessage={({ file }) => `${file.name} wurde nicht hinzugefügt`}
  />
</LocaleProvider>

accessibility:
- **One control:** the native file input, the zone's one tab stop, named by the zone's text and
  by a `label` through `htmlFor`. The browser reports its state itself ("No file chosen", "2
  files"), in its own language.
- **Not drag only:** a click on the zone, or Enter or Space on the input, opens the picker, so
  dropping is never the only way to choose a file (WCAG 2.5.7 and 2.1.1). Dropping needs a pointer
  and a desktop; on phones the picker is the way in.
- **Descriptions:** the input's `aria-describedby` points at the `hint`, at the refusals while
  there are any, and at the Field `message`, after any ids you pass.
- **Announcements:** additions ("report.pdf added", "2 files added"), refusals and removals are
  announced politely through a status region, since a screen reader can't see the list change.
  Nothing is announced while a file is dragged over the zone.
- **The list:** a `<ul>` with a row per file, each with a real remove button named "Remove" and
  the file's name. After a removal, focus moves to the next row's button, the one before, or the
  input.
- **Drag states:** the zone's dashed border turns solid while files are dragged over it, so the
  state shows without color, and in forced colors too. Only the files' types can be read during a
  drag, so the refused look shows only when `accept` names no extension and every type is one it
  refuses; the drop's result is what counts.
- **Forced colors:** the drop target's border takes the system highlight color, and the remove
  buttons keep their circle and cross in the system's button colors, which Bulma's delete button
  otherwise loses there.
- **No ARIA drag attributes:** `aria-dropeffect` and `aria-grabbed` are deprecated, and nothing
  overrides the input's role.
summary: The `Dropzone` component is an area to drop files on or click to pick them, which checks each file and lists the chosen ones with a way to remove each. It's Bulma's boxed, full-width file widget with the real `<input type="file">` lying over it, so the input is the one tab stop, the click target and the drop target, and Enter and Space open the picker. The input holds the chosen files: a pick, drop or paste that passes the checks is written to it, so a form submits the files under `name`. It doesn't upload anything.

parts.summary: The `Dropzone` component is an area to drop files on or click to pick them, which checks each file and lists the chosen ones with a way to remove each. It's Bulma's boxed, full-width file widget with the real `<input type="file">` lying over it, so the input is the one tab stop, the click target and the drop target, and Enter and Space open the picker. The input holds the chosen files: a pick, drop or paste that passes the checks is written to it, so a form submits the files under `name`. It doesn't upload anything.

props.name: label
props.description: Field label, rendered above the zone. It names the input along with the zone's own text, through `htmlFor` (your `id` when you pass one). Inside an outer `Field` it's dropped, and that `Field`'s label names the input.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Props for the label element. An explicit `htmlFor` here overrides the automatic association (no id is generated then).

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the zone, as `File` takes it.

props.name: size
props.description: Size modifier for the zone.

props.name: buttonLabel
props.description: The zone's text. It's the input's accessible name, so keep it short, and put details such as "PDF up to 5 MB" in `hint`. Default: "Choose or drop a file", or "Choose or drop files" with `multiple`.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon above the zone's text. It sits inside the `<label>` that names the input, so leave an `Icon` here unnamed (`<Icon name="upload" />`).

props.name: hint
props.description: A line under the zone that describes the input through `aria-describedby`, such as "PDF up to 5 MB".

props.name: maxSize
props.description: The largest file it takes, in bytes. A bigger one is refused with `file-too-large`.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: With `multiple`, how many files the list holds at most. A drop that would go over adds files up to the limit and refuses the rest with `too-many-files`.

props.name: files
props.description: The chosen files, to control the list. The input and the list follow it, and a change you don't take through `onFilesChange` is undone. Setting it to `[]` clears both.

props.name: onFilesChange
props.description: Called with the whole list of chosen files each time it changes.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Called with the files a pick, drop or paste refused, and why.

props.name: showFileList
props.description: Shows the chosen files under the zone, each with its size and a remove button. Turn it off to show them your own way from `onFilesChange`. The refusals still show.

props.name: allowPaste
props.description: Takes files pasted while the input has focus, through the same checks as a drop.

props.name: preventDocumentDrop
props.description: While it's on the page, stops the browser opening a file dropped outside any drop target, which would leave the page. Drops on other file inputs and on editable fields are left alone.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: Names a file's remove button, for localization. Default: `` `Remove ${file.name}` ``.

props.name: rejectionMessage
props.description: The text shown and announced for a refused file, for localization. Default: the file's name and the reason, such as "photo.png: only PDF files".

props.name: addedMessage
props.description: What's announced when files are added, for localization. Default: the file's name and "added", or a count ("2 files added").

props.name: removedMessage
props.description: What's announced when a file is removed, for localization. Default: `` `${file.name} removed` ``.

props.name: message
props.description: Help or validation message under the Dropzone. It describes the input through `aria-describedby`, after the hint and any refusals.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the root.

props.name: labelSize
props.description: Size for the label (used in horizontal layouts).

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Horizontal field layout.

props.name: messageColor
props.description: Bulma color for the message.

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Field wrapper.

extraProps.name: accept
extraProps.description: File types it takes, as the native attribute writes them (`.pdf`, `image/*`, `application/pdf`). The picker offers them, and Dropzone checks every pick, drop and paste against them by the same rules, since browsers don't check a dropped file. It goes by a file's name and type, not its contents.

extraProps.name: multiple
extraProps.description: Takes several files, and each pick, drop or paste adds to the list. Without it, a new file replaces the one chosen.

extraProps.name: name
extraProps.description: The files' name in the form's data. The input holds the chosen files, so a plain form submit, `FormData` and React 19 actions all carry them.

extraProps.name: required
extraProps.description: The browser's own check: a form won't submit with no file chosen.

extraProps.name: disabled
extraProps.description: Disables the input, hides the remove buttons and takes no drops. A disabled `Fieldset` around it does the same.

extraProps.name: onChange
extraProps.description: Called on the input's `change`, after each pick, drop, paste or removal that changes the files, with `event.target.files` holding the new list.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Forwarded to the `<input>`, so `ref.current.showPicker()` opens the picker from a button of your own. A script that writes the input through it, such as `value = ''` to clear it or a form library setting `files`, changes what the input holds and what the next pick, drop or paste adds to, but no event reports the write, so the list shows it only from the next change. To clear the list at once, reset the form, or control it with `files` and set that to `[]`.

parts.catchAll: All standard <input> attributes and Bulma helper props
parts.helperPropsNote: Helper props go on the `.dropzone` root `<div>`, with `className`. The other attributes go on the `<input>`.
